passages.heading: Its revelation
passages.text: Allah Almighty revealed it piecemeal in 23 years in Makkah and Madeenah.

passages.heading: What Is the Qur’an?
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is the Word of Allah Almighty that He revealed to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. It is the last of Allah’s revealed books, and there is no other book after it.

The revealed books are the books that Allah Almighty revealed to His prophets.
A Muslim believes that these books were revealed by Allah Almighty, and that Allah spoke in them in a manner that befits Him. These books include Az-Zaboor (the Psalms), which He revealed to Daawood (David) عليه السلام; At-Tawraat (the Torah), which He revealed to Moosaa (Moses) عليه السلام and Al-Injeel (the Gospel), which He revealed to Jesus, عليه السلام. All these books have undergone alteration and corruption through the ages.

passages.heading: Its source
passages.text: Allah Almighty revealed it to His Messenger ﷺ through Gabriel ؑ.

passages.heading: Its language
passages.text: Allah Almighty revealed it in Arabic.

passages.heading: The Qur’an is a Way of Life
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is the Word of the Lord of all the worlds, who has created all mankind, knows them better than they know themselves and knows what benefits them and what harms them, hence the reason why Allah Almighty has made the Qur’an, which was the last of His revealed books, a didactic book which maps out a way of life for people, as evidenced by the following points:

- It deals with human life extensively, taking into account its three intrinsic spheres: personal life, family life and community life.
- Its deals with a wide array of matters, including, among other things, beliefs, acts of worship, customs, social and financial relations, man’s mental, emotional and physical states, international relations and peace and war.
- It promotes justice under all circumstances, even when dealing with enemies, and forbids injustice in all its forms.

> The Holy Qur’an maps out the way of life for people and defines and explains to them their rights and obligations with great flexibility, making its laws valid for all times and places.

passages.heading: Its miraculous nature
passages.text: The Arab unbelievers rejected the Qur’an, so Allah challenged them to produce the like of it, or one soorah like it, or even ten verses, but they were unable to do so.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: When Allah sent prophets to their people to call them to the truth, he supported them with some miracles to prove to them that they were true prophets. These miracles, however, ended with the passing of these prophets. As for the Messenger of Islam ﷺ, Allah also furnished him with certain miracles to show his people, and all mankind, for that matter, but the greatest of all of them was His Glorious Book, which He took upon Himself to preserve even after the demise of His prophet ﷺ. In this lesson, we are going to learn about some virtues and etiquette associated with the Qur’an.

passages.heading: Stories of the Prophets in the Qur’an
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is replete with stories of the previous prophets and their people, starting with Adam, and passing through Noah, Hud, Saalih, Shu’ayb, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Jesus, and other prophets and messengers, peace be upon them all. The Holy Qur’an mentions their stories for a number of reasons, including the following:

- to show that the religion of all the prophets is, in essence, the same and that its basis is to worship Allah Almighty alone.
- to give solace to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and make him stand firm and steadfast, reminding him that prophets before him suffered the same hardships he himself was experiencing.
- to give comfort and solace to the believers, reminding them that even Allah’s honourable servants before them were afflicted with trials and tribulations.
- to afford people the opportunity to learn lessons from such true stories.

passages.heading: Its names
passages.text: Allah calls it Al-Qur’aan (the Qur’an), *Al-Kitaab* (the Book), *Al-Furqaan* (the Criterion) and *Adh-Dhhikr* (the Remembrance). It has several other names.

passages.heading: Its Major Themes
passages.text:
The most important themes the Holy Qur’an deals with include:
- Allah’s unity and the refutation of associating partners with Him
- The universe, whose perfect creation bears witness to its Creator, Exalted be He.
- Qura’nic stories, which are replete with lessons and admonitions.
- The beginning of creation and the resurrection on Judgement Day, when Allah will repay all according to their deeds.
- Enlightening the believers and laying down laws for them

passages.heading: The Virtue of Reading/Reciting the Qur’an
passages.text:
- The Prophet ﷺ said, “If anyone reads/recites one single letter in Allah’s Book, he will be credited with a good deed, and a good deed gets a tenfold reward. I do not say that *alif*, *laam*, *meem* are one letter; rather, *alif* is a letter, *laam* is a letter and *meem* is a letter” (Reported by At-Tirmidhee; No. 2910 with an authentic chain of narrators).

- The Prophet ﷺ also said, “Read the Qur’an, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for those who read it.” (Reported by Muslim; No. 804).

passages.heading: Lesson 1
passages.text: ## Learn about the Holy Qur’an

passages.heading: The Qur’an is Food for the Soul and Mind
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an addresses both people’s minds and souls. It addresses the mind by:

- encouraging them to use logical reasoning on the various issues. The Almighty says, {{Q:21:22}} (Soorat Al-Anbiyyaa’, 21:22).
- calling them to exercise their intellects and contemplate His signs and the proofs of His power. The Almighty says, {{Q:2:219}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:219).
- reproving those who do not use their intellects to reflect on His signs. The Almighty says, {{Q:25:44}} (Soorat Al-Furqaan, 25: 44).

It also addresses the soul and emotions by:

- spotlighting and depicting human feelings in many cases. The Almighty says, {{Q:2:165}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:165).
- calling attention to human emotions and pointing out their good and bad effects. The Almighty says, {{Q:5:82}} (Soorat Al-Maa’idah, 5:82).
- commanding Muslims to exercise kindness and gentleness when inviting others to Islam. The Almighty says, {{Q:16:125}} (Soorat An-Nahl, 16: 125).
- incorporating aspects of faith into verses on legal rules. The Almighty says, {{Q:4:94}} (Soorat An-Nisaa’, 4:94).
- using moving words that evoke genuine emotions. The Almighty says, {{Q:24:22}} (Soorat An-Noor, 24:22).

passages.heading: Levels of Worship
The Position of the Prayer in Islam
passages.text:
The prayer has a number of distinctive characteristics, including the following:

- It is the second pillar of Islam after the two testimonies of faith.
- It is the act of worship that must be performed under all circumstances, in times of war and peace, and whether one is sick or in good health.
- It is the act of worship that distinguishes a Muslim from a non-Muslim.

passages.heading: Why Do We Pray?
passages.text: We pray because the prayer is an act of worship that Allah has enjoined on Muslims.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: The prayer is the greatest religious duty that a Muslim must learn and perform. Allah’s Messenger ﷺ has taught us how to perform it in the manner most pleasing to Allah Almighty. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the obligatory prayers, the position of the prayer in Islam, its conditions, and the correct manner of performing it.

passages.heading: The Five Obligatory Prayers
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform five prayers throughout the day and night, namely:

| The Prayer | Beginning Time | Ending Time | Number of units (*rak‘ahs*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *Fajr* (Dawn) Prayer | at the break of dawn | sunrise | 2 |
| *Dhuhr* (Midday) Prayer | when the sun starts declining westward at midday after reaching its zenith | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | 4 |
| *‘Asr* (Late Afternoon) Prayer | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | sunset | 4 |
| *Maghrib* (Sunset) Prayer | sunset | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | 3 |
| *‘Ishaa’* (Late Evening) Prayer | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | midnight | 4 |

passages.heading: The Meaning of the Prayer
passages.text:
The prayer: It is a daily act of worship that consists of a set of words and actions with which a Muslim seeks to draw closer to his Lord, and it is performed five times a day and night.

The prayer is the second pillar of Islam.

passages.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
passages.text:
To perform the prayer, several conditions must be met:
There are several conditions required to perform the prayer, which are:

passages.heading: The Prayer
passages.text:
11. He turns his face to his right and says: Assalaamu ‘alaykum wa rahmatullaah “May Allah’s peace and mercy be upon you.” Then he turns his face to his left and says the same this. With this, he concludes his prayer.

This manner only applies to a prayer that consists of two units (*rak’ahs*), such as *Fajr* and *Jumu’ah* prayers. If, however, the prayer consists of three units (*rak’ahs*), namely *Maghrib*, or four units (*rak’ahs*), namely *Dhuhr*, *‘Asr* and *‘Ishaa’*, he completes the remaining units after concluding the first *tashahhud*, in the same way he has performed the first *rak’ah* but without reciting anything else after *Soorat Al-Faatihah*, then sits as he has done after the second *rak’ah*, recites the first *tashahhud* and *As-Salaatu Al-Ibraaheemiyyah*, and then concludes the prayer by saying, Assalaamu ‘alaykum wa rahmatullaah May Allah’s peace and mercy be upon you.” first to the right and then to the left.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: What will a person who shows off his acts of worship lose by not intending to do them for the sake of Allah?

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of the Prayer:
passages.text:
- It is the direct, special and personal communion a Muslim establishes with his Lord.
- It relieves the mind of worry and all worldly anxieties.
- It strengthens a Muslim’s willpower and determination.
- It refines morals and keeps those who observe it away from evil.

passages.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
passages.text:
- Purity: Once’s body and the place where the prayer is to be performed must be cleansed from physical impurities, and any ritual impurity must be removed with *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.
- Covering the intimate parts of the body (*‘awrah*): The word *‘awrah* refers to the parts of the body that must be covered in front of people. A man’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer extends from the navel to the knees; a woman’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer is her entire body except for the face and hands.
- Facing the *qiblah*: The *qiblah* is the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah. One must, therefore, pray in the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah.
- When its appointed time becomes due: The prayer will not be valid if it is performed before its time has started. It is not permissible to delay it beyond its due time, and it is best to perform it at the beginning of its time.

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text: If a Muslim wants to pray, he must do the following:

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to pray.
2. He stands facing the *qiblah*, raises his hands up to the level of the shoulders or ears, and says, “*Allaahu akbar* Allah is the Greatest.”
3. He places his right hand on his left hand. Then he recites one of the opening supplications, such as, Subhaanak-Allaahumma wa bi hamdika, wa tabaarak-asmuka, wa ta’aalaa jadduka, wa laa ilaaha ghayruka “Glory be to You, O Allah; Yours is the praise, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.” Then he says, A’oodhu billaahi min-ash-shaytaan-ir-rajeem. Bismillaah-ir-rahmaan-ir-raheem “I seek Allah’s protection from Satan, who has been expelled from His mercy. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Then he recites *Soorat Al-Faatihah* and says after it, “*Aameen*”, which means “Answer our supplications, O Allah”. After that, he recites whatever number of verses of the Qur’an as is easy for him, even if it is one verse.
4. He says, “Allaahu akbar Allah is the Greatest” while raising his hands up to the level of his shoulders or ears, and bows down, lowering his head and back and keeping them straight at a right angle, placing the palms of his hands on the knees. He says three times while in this position, “Subhaana rabbiy-al-’adheem Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty.”

passages.heading: The Prayer
passages.text: 10. After the second prostration in the second unit (*rak’ah*), he takes a sitTheting posture and says, “All reverence, all the prayers and all the good things are due to Allah. Peace be on you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be on us and all the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that none is worthy of worship except Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger.” This is called the first *tashahhud*. Then he recites the following, “O Allah, exalt Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You have exalted Abraham and the family of Abraham. Verily, You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You have blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham. Verily, You are Praiseworthy and Glorious.” This is called, “*As-Salaatu Al-Ibraaheemiyyah*.’

passages.heading: The Friday Prayer (Salaat-ul-Jumu’ah)
passages.text:
- Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform a special prayer on Friday, called *Salaat-ul-Jumu’ah* (the Friday prayer). It is performed in a special manner, has special conditions and takes the place of the daily *Dhuhr* (midday) prayer on this day.
- Muslims gather together to perform it in the mosque. The *imaam* delivers a two-section *khutbah* (sermon), then he leads them in a two-*rak’ahs* prayer in which he recites the Qur’an aloud.
- It is recommended to take a ritual bath (*ghusl*) to attend the Friday prayer and proceed early to the mosque. It is not permissible to miss it without a legitimate excuse, and if for any reason a person misses it he must perform the four-unit *Dhuhr* (midday) prayer instead but without reciting the Qur’an aloud.
- Women and people on a journey are exempt from performing the Friday prayer.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text:
Discuss with your classmates some of the challenges facing Muslims that prevent them from performing the prayers on time, and how to overcome these challenges.

passages.heading: What Is the Qur’an?
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is the Word of Allah Almighty that He revealed to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. It is the last of Allah’s revealed books, and there is no other book after it.

The revealed books are the books that Allah Almighty revealed to His prophets.
A Muslim believes that these books were revealed by Allah Almighty, and that Allah spoke in them in a manner that befits Him. These books include Az-Zaboor (the Psalms), which He revealed to Daawood (David) عليه السلام; At-Tawraat (the Torah), which He revealed to Moosaa (Moses) عليه السلام and Al-Injeel (the Gospel), which He revealed to Jesus, عليه السلام. All these books have undergone alteration and corruption through the ages.

passages.heading: What Are Financial Transactions?
passages.text: A financial transaction is an agreement which involves the exchange a valuable property (*maal*), whether in exchange for another form a valuable property, such as a sale, or in exchange for a usufruct (a legal right to use and derive profit from property belonging to someone else provided that the property itself is not injured in any way), such as leasing, or in exchange for nothing at all, such as a gift.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Islam is the religion with which Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ and is an extension of the same religion with which all the previous messengers came. It is essentially based on the belief that Allah Almighty is the only deity deserving of worship, who has no partners or assistants whatsoever in His kingdom, and who has no intermediaries between Him and His servants. But why should I embrace Islam? Is it a religion for all people or is it only for the Arabs? Who is its prophet, and is there another prophet who will come after him?

passages.heading: Its names
passages.text: Allah calls it Al-Qur’aan (the Qur’an), *Al-Kitaab* (the Book), *Al-Furqaan* (the Criterion) and *Adh-Dhhikr* (the Remembrance). It has several other names.

passages.heading: The Virtue of Reading/Reciting the Qur’an
passages.text:
- The Prophet ﷺ said, “If anyone reads/recites one single letter in Allah’s Book, he will be credited with a good deed, and a good deed gets a tenfold reward. I do not say that *alif*, *laam*, *meem* are one letter; rather, *alif* is a letter, *laam* is a letter and *meem* is a letter” (Reported by At-Tirmidhee; No. 2910 with an authentic chain of narrators).

- The Prophet ﷺ also said, “Read the Qur’an, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for those who read it.” (Reported by Muslim; No. 804).

passages.heading: The Blessed Month of Ramadaan
passages.text:
Ramadaan is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar. It is a blessed month, in which Allah revealed the Qur’an to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. Allah has promised to forgive all the past sins of those who fast during the daylight hours and stands in prayer at night throughout this month. The Almighty has also distinguished it with a night that is better than a thousand months. It is called *Laylat-ul-Qadr* (The Night of Decree; also called the Night of Power), and whoever spends it remembering Allah and standing in prayer will have all his past sins forgiven.

Muslims perform the *Taraaweeh* prayer in the month of Ramadaan. It is one of the Prophet’s practices (*Sunnah*) that is particularly associated with it, and it is performed after *'Ishaa’* (late evening) prayer.

passages.heading: What Are the Conditions for Islamic Slaughter?
passages.text:
Islamic slaughter is one that satisfies the following conditions:

1. The person undertaking the slaughtering process must be Muslim, Jew or Christian who has reached the age of discretion and carries out this act for the intended purpose.
2. The tool used for slaughter must be suitable for the intended purpose, causes blood to flow and sharp, such as a knife. It is forbidden to use anything that may kill the animal due to its heavy weight, hit its head to death or render it unconscious by resorting to electric stunning, for instance.
3. The name of Allah must be pronounced by saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) at the time of slaughtering the animal.
4. Cutting what must be cut in the Islamic slaughter, namely, the oesophagus, the throat, and the two jugular veins, or just three of these four.

passages.heading: Allah Almighty has forbidden different types of food and drink, including the following:
passages.text:
- Alcohol, because it clouds the mind; indeed, preserving the mind is one of the objectives of Islamic law (*Sharee’ah*).
- Drugs, because they destroy the mind and body.
- Animals that die without having been slaughtered, or those that are slaughtered but the name of Allah (i.e., saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) was not mentioned at the time of slaughter.
- Pork—and indeed any of the pig’s body parts and by-products—because it is impure and thus forbidden for human consumption.
- Predatory animals, such as lions, tigers, hawks and eagles.
- Any animals that are sacrificed to false deities, such as idols.

The objectives of *Sharee’ah*: This is one of Islamic sciences by which Islamic laws are determined, such as the reason why Allah has laid down such-and-such a rule.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: When Allah sent prophets to their people to call them to the truth, he supported them with some miracles to prove to them that they were true prophets. These miracles, however, ended with the passing of these prophets. As for the Messenger of Islam ﷺ, Allah also furnished him with certain miracles to show his people, and all mankind, for that matter, but the greatest of all of them was His Glorious Book, which He took upon Himself to preserve even after the demise of His prophet ﷺ. In this lesson, we are going to learn about some virtues and etiquette associated with the Qur’an.

passages.heading: Lesson 1
passages.text: ## Learn about the Holy Qur’an

passages.heading: The Qur’an is Food for the Soul and Mind
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an addresses both people’s minds and souls. It addresses the mind by:

- encouraging them to use logical reasoning on the various issues. The Almighty says, {{Q:21:22}} (Soorat Al-Anbiyyaa’, 21:22).
- calling them to exercise their intellects and contemplate His signs and the proofs of His power. The Almighty says, {{Q:2:219}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:219).
- reproving those who do not use their intellects to reflect on His signs. The Almighty says, {{Q:25:44}} (Soorat Al-Furqaan, 25: 44).

It also addresses the soul and emotions by:

- spotlighting and depicting human feelings in many cases. The Almighty says, {{Q:2:165}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:165).
- calling attention to human emotions and pointing out their good and bad effects. The Almighty says, {{Q:5:82}} (Soorat Al-Maa’idah, 5:82).
- commanding Muslims to exercise kindness and gentleness when inviting others to Islam. The Almighty says, {{Q:16:125}} (Soorat An-Nahl, 16: 125).
- incorporating aspects of faith into verses on legal rules. The Almighty says, {{Q:4:94}} (Soorat An-Nisaa’, 4:94).
- using moving words that evoke genuine emotions. The Almighty says, {{Q:24:22}} (Soorat An-Noor, 24:22).

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: One of the aspects of the greatness of Islam is that it covers all facets of human endeavour, including the great care it takes to control people’s dealings with one another, safeguard their rights and prevent them from being subjected to any form of injustice. Part of this care lies in the fact that it has laid down rules and criteria that govern financial transactions. In this lesson, we are going to learn about a set of Islamic rulings pertaining to financial transactions, and the reasons why some of them are prohibited.

passages.heading: The General Islamic Rule Regarding Financial Transactions in Islam
passages.text:
The general Islamic rule is that all types of transactions are permissible, and that none of them is forbidden unless declared as such in the Qur’an or the Prophet’s *Sunnah*.

> The general Islamic rule regarding transactions in general, including financial transactions, is that they are permissible, and thus nothing is considered impermissible without evidence, as opposed to acts of worship, where the general rule regarding them is that they are not permissible unless there is evidence which states otherwise.

passages.heading: Prohibited Forms of Financial Transactions
passages.text:
**Allah Almighty has forbidden some financial transactions, including the following:**

- The unlawful taking of other people’s property, such as by using deceptive tricks or by force.
- Conducting a transaction under coercion, such as by forcing someone to enter into a transaction against his will.
- Trafficking in substances that are injurious to human health, such as alcohol, drugs and tobacco.
- Charging interest on loans, an example of which is to lend money to someone on condition that the borrower must pay, say, 5% on the borrowed amount to the lender.
- Selling things that are not known, such as selling a box the contents of which are unknown.
- Gambling and betting whereby the winner unlawfully takes the money of the loser.

passages.heading: The Reasons for the Prohibition of Financial Transactions
passages.text:
The main reasons for the prohibition of financial transactions are:

1. Injustice
2. Usury (interest)
3. Ignorance and uncertainty (*gharar*) and gambling

passages.heading: Why Should I Embrace Islam?
passages.text:
Some people may ask: Why should I embrace Islam?

The answer is: I must do so for a number of reasons, including the following:

1. Islam is the religion that Allah has approved and chosen for His servants and will not accept any other religion. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85).

2. Islam is the religion of all the prophets and commands its adherents to believe in all of them without exception. Allah says, {{Q:2:136}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:136).
The difference between prophets lies only in the laws relating to people’s actions, as the Almighty says, {{Q:5:48}} (Soorat Al-Maa’idah, 5:48) That is, for each nation before Islam, Allah appointed a law to which people referred for their disputes and a way of life whereby they drew near to Him. Thus, followers of every prophet had their respective laws and regulations, but the set of beliefs to which prophets called their people was the same. Then Allah sent the last prophet and messenger, Muhammad ﷺ, with the final divine laws, and thus the only religion acceptable to Allah is Islam.

3. Islam is the way to happiness in this life and salvation in the life to come; therefore, those who believe in Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and follow him after his message has reached them will be saved; as for those who deny him, they will be doomed to divine punishment. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (*Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85*) The Prophet ﷺ also said, “By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, any person of this Community, Jew or Christian, who hears of me and dies without believing in what I have been sent with will be among the dwellers of Hell” (*Saheeh Muslim;* No. 153).

4. Islam gives conclusive answers to the big questions of human existence: Where did we come from? Why are we here? Where do we go after death?

5. Islam is in perfect harmony with the innate human nature (*fitrah*), beginning with the greatest value it embraces, namely the declaration of Allah’s unity, and ending with the rules of etiquette it teaches its adherents to enable them to attain great perfection in moral excellence.

passages.heading: Its revelation
passages.text: Allah Almighty revealed it piecemeal in 23 years in Makkah and Madeenah.

passages.heading: Its Major Themes
passages.text:
The most important themes the Holy Qur’an deals with include:
- Allah’s unity and the refutation of associating partners with Him
- The universe, whose perfect creation bears witness to its Creator, Exalted be He.
- Qura’nic stories, which are replete with lessons and admonitions.
- The beginning of creation and the resurrection on Judgement Day, when Allah will repay all according to their deeds.
- Enlightening the believers and laying down laws for them

passages.heading: The Types of People Who Are Exempt from Fasting
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has permitted several types of people to break their fast during the day in Ramadaan. They are:

1. Sick people whose medical condition is bound to be further worsened by fasting.
2. The elderly who are unable to fast.
3. Travellers, while moving from one place to another.
4. Menstruating women and women experiencing postnatal bleeding.
5. Pregnant and nursing mothers if they fear it would be dangerous for them or for their babies if they fast.

Islam has made it the husband’s duty to spend on those women entitled to his support without attempting in the least to remind them of his favours.

passages.text:

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Menstrual and Postnatal Bleeding
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has prescribed several rulings relating to menstruating women and women experiencing their postnatal bleeding, including the following:

- They are exempt from performing the prayers during this period and do not have to make up for the prayers they have missed while in this state after the end of menstrual and postnatal bleeding.
- They are exempt from fasting and are not allowed to fast while in this state, but they must make up for the fasting days they have missed in Ramadaan.
- During this period, a husband must not have intercourse with his wife during her menstrual or postnatal period. He is allowed, however, to satisfy his sexual desire but without having intercourse.
- At the end of the menstrual and postnatal period, when bleeding stops completely, women must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*).

passages.heading: What Is Fasting?
passages.text:
Fasting: an act of worship whereby a Muslim abstains from food, drink and sexual intercourse from dawn to sunset.

Fasting in the month of Ramadaan is the fourth pillar of Islam.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Fasting is one of the acts of worship that Allah Almighty has enjoined on all nations. In Islam, a Muslim performs this religious duty in obedience to Allah Almighty. In this lesson, we are going to learn about what fasting means, the things that render it invalid and some of the most important rulings regarding it.

passages.heading: Important Notes Related to Fasting
passages.text:
- Whoever breaks his fast in Ramadaan for a legitimate reason must make up for every day he has missed after than Ramadaan.
- If a sick person breaks the fast because of an incurable disease, he is exempt from fasting the month of Ramadaan, but he must feed one poor person for each day he does not fast.
- If a Muslim cannot possibly fast due to old age, he is exempt from fasting the month of Ramadaan but he must feed one poor person for each day he does not fast.

**Muslims break their fast as soon as the call to *Maghrib* (sunset) prayer is announced, and many Muslims are very keen to share their Ramadaan breakfast, or *iftar*, with fellow Muslims.**

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of Fasting
passages.text:
- To attain true piety by increasing acts of worship and avoiding sins as much as possible.
- To experience the pangs of hunger from which the poor and needy often suffer.
- To train oneself to bring one’s whims and desires under control.

Allah has enjoined fasting on Muslims, just as He prescribed it on the other nations before them:
{{Q:2:183}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:183).

passages.heading: Muslim Women’s Modest Style of Dress (*Hijaab*)
passages.text:
Allah enjoins women to wear the *hijaab* because women enjoy natural beauty and attraction that could easily tempt men into sinful acts, more than the other way round. Women are to cover their entire bodies when in the presence of men who are not related to them, and they may choose any design or colour they like for their *hijaab* as long as the following four conditions are met:

| First Condition | Second Condition | Third condition | Fourth Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| It must appropriately cover the parts of the body that must be covered in public. | It must hang loose and must not fit very closely to the body so that the shape of the body is not revealed. | It must not allow the wearer’s body to be seen through its fabric. | It must not be a type of clothing that is generally considered attractive. |

passages.text: Muslims fast in obedience to Allah Almighty and in response to His command.

passages.text:

“Say: Unbelievers!”

Say, Messenger, to those who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger: You unbelievers.

I do not worship the false gods, such as idols, that you worship.

nor do you worship the True God whom I worship, and who alone is worthy of worship.

passages.heading: Some Distinguishing Characteristics of Islam
passages.text: Islam is distinguished from other religions by many characteristics, the most prominent of which are:

passages.heading: 1 Islam is a Universal Religion
passages.text: Islam is not only for the Arabs; rather, it is the religion that Allah Almighty has approved for all mankind. Addressing His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, the Almighty says, {{Q:21:107}} (*Soorat Al-Anbiyaa’, 21:107*). Thus, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is a mercy to all people without exception, guiding them to the path of faith; and, of all laws, his law reflects all aspects of mercy for people.

passages.heading: *Soorat An-Naas* Explained
passages.text:
“Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind”

Say, Messenger, “I seek refuge and protection in Allah, the Lord of all mankind, who alone has power over all things.

“the King of mankind”

The King of all people, who manages all their affairs.

“the God of mankind”

The True God of all people, who alone deserves to be worshipped by them.

from the harm of Satan who whispers evil suggestions to people when they are heedless of Allah and refrains from doing so when they remember Him.

passages.heading: Lesson 2
passages.text: ## The Interpretation of Short *Surahs*

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Kawthar (Abundant Good)
passages.text:
*Soorat Al-Kawthar* **Explained**

{{Q:108:1-3}}

“We have bestowed on you abundant good”

We have given you, Messenger, immeasurable, abundant good in this life and the life to come, part of which is River Al-Kawthar in Paradise.

“So pray to your Lord and sacrifice to Him”

Therefore, sincerely pray to your Lord and worship Him alone, and sacrifice to Him, pronouncing Allah’s name alone when slaughtering animals, in gratitude to Him for the honour and good He has bestowed on you.

“He who hates you is the one who is truly cut off”

*Shaani’aka*: The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought.

The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought is the most disgraced and contemptible, whose mention is short-lived and who is cut off from all good.

passages.heading: 2 Islam Wipes out the Sins Committed before It
passages.text: If a person sincerely embraces Islam, the Most Gracious and the Most Merciful God will forgive him all his past sins, and this is one of the outstanding merits of Islam. The Almighty says to His Prophet ﷺ, {{Q:8:38}} (Soorat Al-Anfaal, 8:38). A man once showed interest in Islam, and so he went to the Prophet ﷺ but he stipulated that Allah should forgive him his past sins. The Prophet ﷺ gave him the good news, saying, “Don’t you know that Islam wipes out all the sins committed before it?” (Reported by Muslim; No. 121).

passages.heading: Who is the prophet of Islam?
passages.text: Muslims believe that Muhammad ﷺ is the Last Prophet whom Allah has sent to all mankind to call them to worship Allah alone and to declare that Muhammad is His Last Prophet. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:33:40}} (Soorat Al-Ahzaab, 33:40)

passages.heading: Learning Your religion
passages.text:
- A Muslim is required to learn his religion based on sound knowledge in order to worship his Lord properly.
- The Prophet ﷺ urges us to study and understand our religion. He once said, “When Allah wishes to bestow His favour on someone, He makes him understand the religion.” (Reported by Al-Bukhaaree; No. 71).
- The Prophet ﷺ states that acquiring religious knowledge leads to Paradise. He once said, “Whoever treads a path in search of knowledge, Allah will ease the way to Paradise for him.” (Saheeh Ibn Hibbaan; No. 84).

passages.heading: The Criterion of Superiority in Islam
passages.text:
Piety is the criterion whereby Allah grants superiority to some over others. Superiority among Muslims can only be attained through strong faith, not one’s appearance, lineage, colour, or wealth. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:49:13}} (Soorat Al-Hjuraat, 49:13).

The Prophet ﷺ said: “O people! Your Lord is one and your father [Adam] is one. An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor does a non-Arab have any superiority over an Arab; a white person has no superiority over a black person, nor does a black person have any superiority over a white person except in piety.” (Reported by Al-Bayhaqee in Shu’ab al-Eemaan; No. 4774).

passages.heading: The Pillars of Faith
passages.text:
The Muslim faith rests on six pillars, namely:

1. **Belief in Allah:** A Muslim believes that Allah Almighty exists and believes in His names and attributes. He equally believes that He is the Lord and sole Creator of this vast universe, to whom belongs everything in it, who manages all its affairs and provides sustenance to all His creation, that there is no god is worthy of worship besides or instead of Him and that He has perfect attributes.
2. **Belief in the angels:** A Muslim believes that the honourable angels exist, that it is Allah Almighty who created them and that they worship Him, execute His commands and never disobey Him. He also believes in their attributes and duties which are mentioned in the Book and the *Sunnah*.

passages.heading: Shirk
passages.text:
3. **Belief in the divinely revealed books:** A Muslim believes that Allah sent down divine books to His Messengers to guide people to the truth and teach them their religion. These include the Torah (*At-Tawraah*) which He revealed to Moses (Moosaa) son of ‘Imraan, the Zaboor which He revealed to David (Daawood), the Gospel (*Al-Injeel*) which He revealed to Jesus (‘Eesaa) son of Mary and the Qur’an which He revealed to Muhammad, peace be upon them all. He also believes that the Qur’an is the last of them and that it has final authority over them all.
4. **Belief in the prophets:** A Muslim believes that Allah Almighty sent messengers to their people and supported them with miracles to prove their truthfulness. He sent them to give the believers good news of reward, warn the unbelievers of punishment and teach their people their religion. Those to whom they were sent must obey and follow them. Muhammad ﷺ was the final prophet whom He sent to all mankind.
5. **Belief in the Last Day:** A Muslim believes in Resurrection Day. He believes that Allah will raise the dead from their graves on that day and judge and repay them according to their deeds. Some will enter Paradise while others will enter Hell.
6. **Belief in the divine decree:** A Muslim believes that everything in this universe, whether good or evil, happens according to Allah’s decree, that He foreknows all events which He has already written in the Preserved Tablet, and that everything in this universe happens according to His will.

passages.heading: Shirk
passages.text: Al-Lawh Al-Mahfoodh (the Preserved Tablet) is the book in which Allah has written everything He has decreed for all creation until the Day of Resurrection.

passages.heading: Benefits of Faith
passages.text:
Faith has many benefits, including the following:

* **Peace and tranquillity:** Faith gives the believer tranquillity and reassurance. He submits to Allah’s decree, or *qadar*, and fears none but Allah.

> Al-Qadar, or divine decree, refers to the things Allah Almighty has already preordained and His foreknowledge that they will occur at times known only to Him and in a particular manner.

passages.heading: Benefits of Faith
passages.text:
* **Getting to know Allah Almighty:** A believer gets to know his Lord and His names, attributes and actions, so much so that he becomes more attached to Him.
* **Glorying Allah:** the more a believer gets to know his Lord, the more he extols and loves Him, the more he hopes for His mercy and the more God-fearing he becomes.
* **Getting to know Allah’s graciousness to His servants:** for sending messengers to them and divine books to them to guide them to the true religion.
* **Loving the angels:** for worshipping Allah and showing obedience to Him.
* **Loving Allah’s Messengers:** Allah Almighty chose them to convey His message to people.
* **Diligent worship:** the stronger the faith, the more worship one performs.
* **A truly happy life:** A believer is content with what Allah has apportioned to him and knows that whatever calamities befall him in this world elevate his rank and efface his sins. He also hopes for the bliss He has prepared for the believers in the life to come.
* **Not to be deluded by this world:** The life of this world is temporary and only serves as a means to eternal life in the hereafter.
* **Exposing myths:** Faith exposes and nullifies many myths.
* **Entering Paradise:** This is the abode of eternal bliss which Allah Almighty has prepared for His believing servants.

passages.heading: 2 Islam Wipes out the Sins Committed before It
passages.text: If a person sincerely embraces Islam, the Most Gracious and the Most Merciful God will forgive him all his past sins, and this is one of the outstanding merits of Islam. The Almighty says to His Prophet ﷺ, {{Q:8:38}} (Soorat Al-Anfaal, 8:38). A man once showed interest in Islam, and so he went to the Prophet ﷺ but he stipulated that Allah should forgive him his past sins. The Prophet ﷺ gave him the good news, saying, “Don’t you know that Islam wipes out all the sins committed before it?” (Reported by Muslim; No. 121).

5. He resumes the standing position, raising his hands up to the level of the shoulders or the ears, saying: Sami’allaahu li man hamidah “Allah hears those who praise Him.” Then he says while standing: Rabbanaa wa lakal-hamd “Our Lord, to You is due all praise.”

6. He says, Allaahu akbar “Allah is the Greatest” and prostrates himself, with the toes of both feet, the knees, the palms of the hands and the forehead and the nose touching the floor. He says three times while in this position, “Glory be to my Lord, Most High.”

passages.heading: The Blessed Month of Ramadaan
passages.text:
Ramadaan is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar. It is a blessed month, in which Allah revealed the Qur’an to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. Allah has promised to forgive all the past sins of those who fast during the daylight hours and stands in prayer at night throughout this month. The Almighty has also distinguished it with a night that is better than a thousand months. It is called *Laylat-ul-Qadr* (The Night of Decree; also called the Night of Power), and whoever spends it remembering Allah and standing in prayer will have all his past sins forgiven.

Muslims perform the *Taraaweeh* prayer in the month of Ramadaan. It is one of the Prophet’s practices (*Sunnah*) that is particularly associated with it, and it is performed after *'Ishaa’* (late evening) prayer.

passages.text:
*Soorat Al-Kawthar* **Explained**

{{Q:108:1-3}}

“We have bestowed on you abundant good”

We have given you, Messenger, immeasurable, abundant good in this life and the life to come, part of which is River Al-Kawthar in Paradise.

“So pray to your Lord and sacrifice to Him”

Therefore, sincerely pray to your Lord and worship Him alone, and sacrifice to Him, pronouncing Allah’s name alone when slaughtering animals, in gratitude to Him for the honour and good He has bestowed on you.

“He who hates you is the one who is truly cut off”

*Shaani’aka*: The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought.

The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought is the most disgraced and contemptible, whose mention is short-lived and who is cut off from all good.

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Ikhlaas Explained
passages.text:
“Say: He is Allah, the One and Only”

Say, Messenger, to those who ask you about your Lord: He is Allah, the One and Only Lord and God, besides whom there is no deity deserving of worship.

“Allah, the Everlasting Sustainer of all”

He is Allah, the Eternal and Absolute God with perfect attributes, to whom all creation turns to fulfil their needs, while He stands in need of none.

“He has not begotten anyone, nor was He Himself begotten by anyone”

He is Allah, who has no offspring whatsoever, neither son nor daughter, and He has no parents, neither father nor mother.

“And none is equal to Him”

And there is no one and nothing among His creation that resembles Him in any way whatsoever with regard to His being, names attributes or actions.

and from the evil of those witches who blow on knots when they practise magic.

passages.heading: Important Notes Related to _Hajj_
passages.text:
- A Muslim cannot perform hajj except in a specific place, namely Makkah, and only at a specific time of the year.
- Hajj includes several acts of worship that a Muslim must learn before going to perform the pilgrimage.

Every year, Muslims from different countries perform hajj in large groups. Donning uniform simple clothing, both rich and poor appear to be the same with all social barriers and distinctions broken down.

passages.heading: The Qur’an is a Way of Life
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is the Word of the Lord of all the worlds, who has created all mankind, knows them better than they know themselves and knows what benefits them and what harms them, hence the reason why Allah Almighty has made the Qur’an, which was the last of His revealed books, a didactic book which maps out a way of life for people, as evidenced by the following points:

- It deals with human life extensively, taking into account its three intrinsic spheres: personal life, family life and community life.
- Its deals with a wide array of matters, including, among other things, beliefs, acts of worship, customs, social and financial relations, man’s mental, emotional and physical states, international relations and peace and war.
- It promotes justice under all circumstances, even when dealing with enemies, and forbids injustice in all its forms.

> The Holy Qur’an maps out the way of life for people and defines and explains to them their rights and obligations with great flexibility, making its laws valid for all times and places.

passages.heading: Stories of the Prophets in the Qur’an
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is replete with stories of the previous prophets and their people, starting with Adam, and passing through Noah, Hud, Saalih, Shu’ayb, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Jesus, and other prophets and messengers, peace be upon them all. The Holy Qur’an mentions their stories for a number of reasons, including the following:

- to show that the religion of all the prophets is, in essence, the same and that its basis is to worship Allah Almighty alone.
- to give solace to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and make him stand firm and steadfast, reminding him that prophets before him suffered the same hardships he himself was experiencing.
- to give comfort and solace to the believers, reminding them that even Allah’s honourable servants before them were afflicted with trials and tribulations.
- to afford people the opportunity to learn lessons from such true stories.

passages.heading: Note
passages.text: Islam respects the customs and traditions of all peoples and does not require them to change them unless they contravene any of the teachings of Islam.

passages.heading: 3 Islam is the Final Religion
passages.text: Allah Almighty has made Islam an extension of the previous divinely revealed religions and has approved and chosen it for all mankind until the end of the world. Thus, it is the only true religion on the face of the earth. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85).

passages.heading: Things that render the Fast Invalid
passages.text:
The fasting person must abstain from several things which, if he does them, his fast will be invalid. They are:

1. Eating and drinking, including intravenous injections which have some nutritional value.
2. Deliberate seminal emission as a result of intercourse or any other means. Intercourse during the day in Ramadaan is a grave sin.
3. Deliberate vomiting.

A woman’s fast is broken as a result of:

4. Menstrual or postnatal bleeding.

passages.heading: The Types of People Who Are Exempt from Fasting
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has permitted several types of people to break their fast during the day in Ramadaan. They are:

1. Sick people whose medical condition is bound to be further worsened by fasting.
2. The elderly who are unable to fast.
3. Travellers, while moving from one place to another.
4. Menstruating women and women experiencing postnatal bleeding.
5. Pregnant and nursing mothers if they fear it would be dangerous for them or for their babies if they fast.

passages.heading: Important Notes Related to Fasting
passages.text:
- Whoever breaks his fast in Ramadaan for a legitimate reason must make up for every day he has missed after than Ramadaan.
- If a sick person breaks the fast because of an incurable disease, he is exempt from fasting the month of Ramadaan, but he must feed one poor person for each day he does not fast.
- If a Muslim cannot possibly fast due to old age, he is exempt from fasting the month of Ramadaan but he must feed one poor person for each day he does not fast.

**Muslims break their fast as soon as the call to *Maghrib* (sunset) prayer is announced, and many Muslims are very keen to share their Ramadaan breakfast, or *iftar*, with fellow Muslims.**

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Islam is the religion with which Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ and is an extension of the same religion with which all the previous messengers came. It is essentially based on the belief that Allah Almighty is the only deity deserving of worship, who has no partners or assistants whatsoever in His kingdom, and who has no intermediaries between Him and His servants. But why should I embrace Islam? Is it a religion for all people or is it only for the Arabs? Who is its prophet, and is there another prophet who will come after him?

passages.heading: Conditions for Acts of Worship to Be Accepted
passages.text:
For an act of worship to be accepted, two conditions must be fulfilled:

The first condition: It has to be done sincerely for the sake of Allah to draw closer to alone, without showing off.

The second condition: It has to be done in the manner Allah has enjoined it and exactly as it was performed by the Prophet ﷺ.

> *Aririyyaa’* (showing off) is the act of doing an act of worship only to be seen and praised by people for doing it.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Meat Served in Restaurants and Shops
passages.text:
1. The meat of animals that are slaughtered by other than a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book (a Christian or a Jew), such as a Buddhist, or a Hindu is strictly forbidden. This includes meat served in restaurants and shops in countries where Muslims or People of the Book constitute a minority.
2. The meat of animals killed by a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book is lawful based on textual evidence to this effect in the Qur’an.
3. The meat of animals that are not killed according to Islamic law, such as by electrocution and drowning, is strictly forbidden.
4. The general rule is that it is permissible to consume the flesh of animals slaughtered by People of the Book as well as meat of animals generally found in their restaurants and shops, making sure, however, to invoke Allah’s name at the time of eating (that is, by saying *Bismillaah*), but it is better for Muslims to eat only meat that has been proven to be lawful (*halaal*).

passages.heading: What is the Islamic Ruling on Seafood Consumption?
passages.text:
It is permissible to eat dead aquatic animals that can live only in water, such as fish and prawns, whether they live in the sea, rivers or lakes.

It is permissible to hunt wild, nonpredatory animals and consume their flesh provided that the name of Allah is mentioned before the hunting weapon is discharged, and the hunted game must be slaughtered if found still alive.

passages.heading: The Pillars of Islam
passages.text:
Islam is built on five pillars:

Every Muslim must strictly adhere to these pillars to ensure he is practising Islam in full; negligence in one of these pillars is bound to render the way you practise Islam deficient.

1. The two testimonies of faith: To bear witness that none is worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is His His Messenger
2. Establish the prayer: A Muslim must pray five times a day. These prayers will be explained in due course.
3. Paying zakaat
4. Fasting in the month of Ramadaan
5. Making the pilgrimage to Allah’s House

passages.heading: Why Should I Embrace Islam?
passages.text:
Some people may ask: Why should I embrace Islam?

The answer is: I must do so for a number of reasons, including the following:

1. Islam is the religion that Allah has approved and chosen for His servants and will not accept any other religion. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85).

2. Islam is the religion of all the prophets and commands its adherents to believe in all of them without exception. Allah says, {{Q:2:136}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:136).
The difference between prophets lies only in the laws relating to people’s actions, as the Almighty says, {{Q:5:48}} (Soorat Al-Maa’idah, 5:48) That is, for each nation before Islam, Allah appointed a law to which people referred for their disputes and a way of life whereby they drew near to Him. Thus, followers of every prophet had their respective laws and regulations, but the set of beliefs to which prophets called their people was the same. Then Allah sent the last prophet and messenger, Muhammad ﷺ, with the final divine laws, and thus the only religion acceptable to Allah is Islam.

3. Islam is the way to happiness in this life and salvation in the life to come; therefore, those who believe in Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and follow him after his message has reached them will be saved; as for those who deny him, they will be doomed to divine punishment. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (*Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85*) The Prophet ﷺ also said, “By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, any person of this Community, Jew or Christian, who hears of me and dies without believing in what I have been sent with will be among the dwellers of Hell” (*Saheeh Muslim;* No. 153).

4. Islam gives conclusive answers to the big questions of human existence: Where did we come from? Why are we here? Where do we go after death?

5. Islam is in perfect harmony with the innate human nature (*fitrah*), beginning with the greatest value it embraces, namely the declaration of Allah’s unity, and ending with the rules of etiquette it teaches its adherents to enable them to attain great perfection in moral excellence.

passages.heading: صلاة الجمعة:
passages.text:
- فرض الله عز وجل على المسلمين أداء صلاة خاصة يوم الجمعة تسمى (صلاة الجمعة)، ولها صفة خاصة وشروط خاصة، وهي بدل عن صلاة الظهر لذلك اليوم.
- يجتمع المسلمون من أجلها في المسجد، يخطب فيهم إمام المسجد خطبتين، ثم يصلي بهم ركعتين، يجهر فيها بقراءة القرآن.
- يشرع الاغتسال لحضور صلاة الجمعة، والتبكير لحضورها. ولا يجوز التخلف عنها إلا لعذر، ومن تخلّف عنها فإنه يصلي صلاة الظهر أربع ركعات، لا يجهر فيها بقراءة القرآن.
- لا تجب صلاة الجمعة على المرأة أو المسافر.

passages.heading: الصلوات الخمس:
passages.text:

passages.heading: صفة الغسل الكامل:
passages.text:
إذا أراد المسلم أن يغتسل غسلاً كاملاً، فعليه القيام بالخطوات الآتية:

1. ينضح فرجه بالماء.
2. يتوضأ مثل وضوء الصلاة.
3. يغسل جميع جسده بالماء.

passages.heading: شهر رمضان المبارك:
passages.text:
هو الشهر التاسع من السنة الهجرية وهو شهرٌ مبارك، أنزل الله فيه القرآن على رسوله محمد ﷺ. وجعل الله تعالى صوم نهاره، والصلاة في ليله سببًا لمغفرة الذنوب. وميَّزه الله تعالى بليلة هي أفضل من ألف شهر، وتسمى (ليلة القدر)، من أحياها بالذكر والصلاة غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه.

يؤدي المسلمون صلاة التراويح في شهر رمضان، وهي من السنن المرتبطة به وتؤدى بعد صلاة العشاء.

passages.heading: نعمة الهداية:
passages.text:
من عرف الحكمة من خلقه، والعاقبة التي تنتظر الناس يوم القيامة، أيقن أن أعظم نعمة ينعم الله بها على عباده هي نعمة الهداية إلى الدين الحق والعمل الصالح.

ولذلك أوجب الله عز وجل على عباده في صلاة أن يسألوه الهداية إلى الطريق المستقيم، الذي هو دين الإسلام، الموصل إلى رضوان الله تعالى.

passages.heading: ما هي الصلاة؟
passages.text:
الصلاة: عبادة يومية، تشتمل على مجموعة من الأقوال والأعمال يتقرب بها العبد إلى ربه، وتؤدى خمس مرات في اليوم.

والصلاة هي الركن الثاني من أركان الإسلام.

passages.heading: كيف نصلي؟
passages.text:
إذا أراد المسلم أن يصلي فعليه القيام بالخطوات الآتية:

1. يستحضر نية الصلاة بقلبه.
2. يقف مستقبلًا القبلة، ويرفع كفيه بجوار كتفيه، ويقول: «الله أكبر».
3. يضع يده اليمنى على يده اليسرى. ثم يقرأ دعاء من أدعية الاستفتاح، مثل: «سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك، وتبارك اسمك، وتعالى جدك، ولا إله غيرك». ثم يقول: «أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم، بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم». ثم يقرأ سورة الفاتحة، ثم يقول: «آمين» عند الانتهاء من قراءتها، ومعناها: اللهم استجب دعاءنا. ثم يقرأ بعد الفاتحة ما تيسّر له مما يحفظ من القرآن الكريم، ولو كان آية واحدة.
4. يرفع يديه بجوار كتفيه أو أذنيه، ويقول: «الله أكبر»، ويحني ظهره راكعًا، ويضع يديه على ركبتيه، ويجعل ظهره ورأسه في مستوى واحد.

ويقول أثناء ركوعه: «سبحان ربي العظيم» ثلاث مرات.

10. بعد السجود الثاني في الركعة الثانية يجلس كجلوسه بين السجدتين، ويقول: «التحيات للَّه والصلوات الطيبات، السلام عليك أيها النبي ورحمة الله وبركاته، السلام علينا وعلى عباد الله الصالحين، أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله»، ويسمى التشهد الأول.

ثم يقول بعده: «اللهم صلِّ على محمد وعلى آل محمد، كما صليت على إبراهيم وعلى آل إبراهيم، إنك حميدٌ مجيد، وبارك على محمد وعلى آل محمد، كما باركت على إبراهيم وعلى آل إبراهيم، إنك حميدٌ مجيد» وتسمى الصلاة الإبراهيمية.

11. يلتفت عن يمينه ويقول: «السلام عليكم ورحمة الله» ثم يلتفت عن شماله ويقول مثل ذلك.

وبذلك تنتهي صلاته.

هذه الصفة إذا كانت صلاته ركعتان؛ كالفجر والجمعة، أما إذا كانت ثلاث ركعات؛ كالمغرب، أو أربع ركعات؛ كالظهر والعصر والعشاء، فإنه بعد الانتهاء من التشهد الأول يكمل ما تبقى من الركعات، ثم يجلس كما جلس بعد الركعة الثانية، ويقول التشهد الأول، ثم يقرأ الصلاة الإبراهيمية على النبي ﷺ، ثم يسلم.

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text:
استعرض مع زملائك بعض التحديات التي تواجه المسلم لتمنعه من أداء الصلاة في وقتها، وكيف يتم تجاوز هذه التحديات؟

{{Q:62:9}} (الجمعة: 9).

اذكر عبادتين من العبادات الخاصة بيوم الجمعة.

ما أثر الصلوات الخمس على حياة المسلم اليومية؟

من خلال زيارتك لهذا الموقع: islamicfiqh.net/en تحدث عن حكم تارك الصلاة في الإسلام

العورة التي يجب على الرجل سترها في الصلاة:
أ) جميع البدن باستثناء الوجه واليدين والقدمين.
ب) من السرة إلى الركبة.
ج) من الكتف إلى الركبة.

الجهة التي يجب على المصلي التوجه لها هي:
أ) جهة الشمال.
ب) جهة الغرب.
ج) جهة الكعبة.

يقول المصلي في سجوده:
أ) سبحان ربي العظيم.
ب) سبحان ربي الأعلى.
ج) رب اغفر لي.

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text: تعتبر الصلاة أعظم شعائر الدين التي يجب على المسلم تعلمها وأدؤها، وقد علمنا رسول الله ﷺ كيفية أدائها بالطريقة التي يرضاها الله عز وجل عنا، وفي هذا الدرس سنتعرف على الصلوات الواجبة، ومنزلتها، وشروطها، وكيفية أدائها بالطريقة الصحيحة.

passages.heading: منزلة الصلاة:
passages.text:
تتميز الصلاة بمجموعة من الخصائص، منها:
- تعد الركن الثاني من أركان الإسلام بعد الشهادتين.
- العبادة التي يجب أداؤها على كل حال، في حال الصحة والمرض، والأمن والخوف.
- العبادة التي يتميّز بها المسلم من الكافر.

passages.heading: لماذا نصلي؟
passages.text:
نصلي لأن الصلاة:

- صلة بين العبد وربه.
- تريح النفس من هموم الدنيا.
- تقوي لدى العبد قوة الإرادة والعزيمة.
- تهذب الأخلاق، وتبعد صاحبها عن المنكرات.

passages.heading: شروط الصلاة:
passages.text:
يشترط لأداء الصلاة عدة شروط، وهي:

- **الطهارة:** وتشمل طهارة البدن والمكان من النجاسات، والطهارة من الحدث بالوضوء أو الغسل.
- **تغطية العورة:** والعورة: ما يجب ستره من البدن أمام الناس. وعورة الرجل التي يجب سترها في الصلاة هي من السرة إلى الركبة، وعورة المرأة التي يجب سترها في الصلاة هي جميع بدنها إلا الوجه والكفّين.
- **استقبال القبلة:** وهي جهة الكعبة المشرفة الموجودة في مكة المكرمة، فيجب على المصلي التوجه إلى جهتها في صلاته.
- **دخول وقت الصلاة:** فلا تصح الصلاة قبل دخول وقتها، ولا يجوز تأخيرها عن وقتها، والأفضل أداؤها في أول وقتها.

5. يرفع رأسه ليعود قائمًا مع رفع يديه إلى جوار كتفيه، وهو يقول: «**سمع الله لمن حمده**». ثم يقول وهو واقف: «**ربنا ولك الحمد**».

6. ينحني ساجدًا على الأرض، فيضع جبهته وأنفه على الأرض، مع وضع كفيه وركبتيه وأطراف أصابع قدميه على الأرض، ويقول: «**سبحان ربي الأعلى**» ثلاث مرات.

passages.heading: ¿Qué tengo que hacer al encontrar agua después de haber realizado la ablución seca (tayamum)?
passages.text: Cuando el musulmán encuentra agua o es capaz de usarla sin causarle daño, en este caso se anula su ablución seca y debe realizar la ablución menor o mayor con agua.

passages.heading: La sura de An-Nas:
passages.text:
{{Q:114:1-6}}

**Exégesis de la sura:**

(Di: “”Me refugio en el Señor de los seres humanos,)

Di -Oh mensajero- me refugio en Al-láh Señor de la gente, el Todopoderoso.

(en el Rey Soberano de los seres humanos,)

El Rey Soberano de toda la gente, Quien maneja todos sus asuntos.

(en el [único] Dios de los seres humanos,)

El Dios de todos los seres humanos, entonces no hay nada ni nadie que merezca ser adorado fuera de Él.

(de la maldad del [demonio] susurrador que huye [cuando el nombre de Dios es mencionado],)

Contra el perjuicio del Satanás quien les susurra cuando dejan de recordar a Al-láh, y deja de susurrar cuando recuerdan a Al-láh.

(que susurra en los corazones de los seres humanos,)

El que esparce malos pensamientos en el pecho de las personas, y manipula sus sentimientos y pensamientos.

(ya sea que pertenezca a los yinn o a los hombres).

De los demonios de los genios y de los humanos.

passages.heading: Lo que se debe hacer en las transacciones financieras:
passages.text:
La base en las transacciones financieras es que están permitidas, y no se prohíben ninguna sino con una prueba legal del Noble Corán o de la sunna profética que indique su prohibición.

La base en las transacciones financieras es que están permitidas, no se prohíben sino con una prueba legal, al contrario de las adoraciones que son invariables (tauquifia) y no se realizan sino es con una prueba legal.

passages.heading: ¿Cómo rezamos?
passages.text: Si el musulmán quiere realizar la oración debe hacer los pasos siguientes:

passages.heading: La manera de realizar la ablución mayor completa:
passages.text:
Si el musulmán quiere realizar la ablución mayor debe hacer los pasos siguientes:

1. Realizar la intención con su corazón (sin pronunciarla) y lavarse la parte íntima con agua.
2. Realizar la ablución menor conocida.
3. Lavar todo su cuerpo con agua.

passages.heading: Normas relacionadas con la menstruación y el posparto.
passages.text:
Al-láh -Enaltecido y Exaltado sea- prescribe unas normas para la mujer menstruante y la en el período de postparto, de las cuales citamos:

■ No rezar, ya que la mujer menstruante no debe rezar en su período de postparto, y no tiene que recuperar los rezos después de su purificación.

■ No ayunar, ya que para la mujer menstruante o en su período de postparto no le está permitido ayunar, pero debe recuperar los días no ayunados después del mes de Ramadán.

■ La prohibición del coito, puesto que es prohibido para el hombre realizar el coito con su esposa estando en su período de menstruación o de postparto y solo se le permite el coito al terminar su período y después de que ella realice la ablución mayor. Está permitido para el esposo acariciar a su esposa en ambos períodos mencionados pero sin llegar a la penetración.

passages.heading: ¿Por qué debo volverme musulmán?
passages.text: Luego Al-láh envió al sello de los profetas y mensajeros: el profeta Muhammad -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- que es el último enviado, su legislación fue la última establecida, por ello no se aceptará ninguna otra religión fuera del Islam.

passages.heading: ¿Qué significan los dos testimonios de fe?
passages.text:
Primero: el significado de “Atestiguo que no hay divinidad digna de ser adorada fuera de Al-láh”.

El significado de (atestiguo que no hay divinidad digna de ser adorada salvo Al-láh): es decir creo sin duda alguna que Al-láh es el Único Dios que merece ser adorado.

Este testimonio incluye dos asuntos

| El primero | El Segundo |
| --- | --- |
| Negar la divinidad a otro fuera de Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- | Afirmar la divinidad para Al-láh unicamente |

passages.heading: Taiámmum (ablución seca):
passages.text: Cuando la persona que debe realizar la ablución menor o mayor es incapaz de realizarlas por la falta de agua, o por una enfermedad u otra causa, en este caso es permitido para él realizar la ablución seca (tayamum). La forma de realizarla es tener la intención en el corazón (sin pronunciarla), tocar con sus dos manos el suelo una sola vez, luego pasar sus manos sobre su cara, luego sus manos.

passages.heading: Segunda lección
passages.text:
### Exégesis de las suras cortas

(del mal de las [hechiceras] sopladoras de nudos,)

Y del mal de las hechiceras, quienes soplan en los nudos para realizar actos de hechicería.;

(y del mal del envidioso cuando envidia)

Y del mal del envidioso quien busca la desaparición de la gracia y el daño para la persona agraciada.

passages.heading: Exégesis de la sura:
passages.text:
(Di: “”¡Oh, incrédulos!)

Di- Oh mensajero- a quienes descreen a Al-láh y a Su mensajero: Oh incrédulos.

(No adoro lo que adoran.)

No adoro lo que adoráis de falsas deidades; como los ídolos y otros.

(Ni adoran ustedes a Quien yo adoro.)

Ustedes no adoran al Dios verdadero que yo adoro, el Único que merece ser adorado.

(Y jamás adoraré lo que adoran.)

Nunca adoraré los falsos dioses que adoran ustedes.

(Ni ustedes adoran a Quien yo adoro.)

Ni ustedes adoran al Dios verdadero quien adoro, el Único que merece ser adorado.

(Ustedes tienen su religión y yo la mía).

Ustedes están aferrados a su religión y yo permanezco aferrado a la mía.

> El incrédulo: es quien rechaza seguir el mensaje del profeta Muhammad -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él-.

passages.heading: A discutir
passages.text: ¿Qué tema enfatizaron las dos suras del Ijlas y la de Al Kafirun?

passages.heading: ¿En qué consisten las transacciones financieras?
passages.text: Las transacciones financieras: son las transacciones en las cuales se intercambian dinero, sea el intercambio de dinero con dinero como la venta, con un beneficio como el arrendamiento, o sin beneficio como un regalo.

passages.heading: Tercera lección
passages.text: ## Las transacciones financieras

passages.heading: Transacciones financieras prohibidas:
passages.text:
Al-láh -Enaltecido y Exaltado sea- ha prohibido algunas transacciones financieras como:

* Tomar injustamente el dinero de la gente; sea por engaño o por coacción.
* Obligar a un comerciante a realizar una transacción que no quiere realizar.
* El tráfico de sustancias nocivas para la salud humana; como el alcohol, las drogas, el tabaco, etc.
* La usura que consiste en prestar dinero con la condición de devolverlo con un aumento, por ejemplo del 5%.
* La venta de lo desconocido, tal como vender una caja que no se sabe lo que hay dentro.
* Los juegos de azar y apuestas en los que el ganador toma injustamente el dinero del perdedor.

passages.heading: Las causas de prohibición de algunas transacciones financieras:
passages.text:
Las causas principales que llevan a la prohibición de una transacción financiera son:

1. La opresión
2. La usura
3. El engaño (gharar)

passages.heading: Las cinco oraciones:
passages.text:
Al-láh -Enaltecido y Exaltado sea- prescribe a sus siervos rezar cinco oraciones al día que son:

| | El inicio de su tiempo | El fin de su tiempo | Sus unidades (Rak’as) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Salat al Fayer (el rezo del alba) | el alba. | el amanecer. | 2 |
| Salat ad-Duhur (el rezo del mediodía): | la puesta del sol (es decir cuando el sol empieza a dirigirse hacia el oeste a mediodía). | cuando se iguala la sombra de una cosa a su longitud. | 4 |
| Salat al- Asr (el rezo de la tarde): | cuando se iguala la sombra de una cosa a su longitud. | el atardecer. | 4 |
| Salat al Magrib (el rezo del ocaso): | el atardecer. | el crepúsculo. | 3 |
| Salat al ‘Isha (el rezo de la noche): | el crepúsculo. | la medianoche. | 4 |

passages.heading: ¿Cómo rezamos?
passages.text:
1. Tener la intención para la oración en su corazón (sin pronunciarla).
2. Ponerse de pie, dirigiéndose hacia la Quibla, levantando sus manos cerca de sus hombros o sus orejas diciendo: “”Al-láhu Akbar””.
3. Poner su mano derecha sobre la izquierda, luego decir la súplica de apertura de la oración (Istiftah) como:”””Glorificado seas Al-láh te alabamos. Bendito sea tu nombre y elevada sea tu majestad. No hay dios sino Tú””.Luego dice:(“”A’udhu bilahi mina shaytanir-rayim”” “”bismilahir-rahmanir-rahim””) es decir (“”Me refugio en Al-láh del maldito Satanás””, “”En el nombre de Al-láh el Clemente el Compasivo””).
Luego recita el capítulo de Al Fatiha y dice “”Amin”” (amén) después de acabarla, es decir: “”Oh Dios mío acepta mis súplicas””Luego recita algo que ha memorizado del Corán, aunque sea una sola aleya.
4. Levanta sus manos hasta sus hombros u orejas diciendo «»Al-láhu Akbar»» luego inclina su espalda poniendo sus manos sobre sus rodillas, estando su espalda y cabeza perpendiculares con sus piernas y dice durante su inclinación: «»Subhana rabial Adhim= Glorificado sea mi Señor Grandioso»» tres veces.

passages.heading: As-Salat (el rezo ritual)
passages.text:
5. Al levantar su cabeza y elevando sus manos cerca de sus hombros dice ‘”Samia’ Al-láhu liman hamidahu= Al-láh escucha quien lo alaba’” y al estar de pie dice: ‘”Rabana walakal Hamd= Señor mío a Ti pertenecen las alabanzas’”.

6. Luego prosterna poniendo su frente, su nariz, las palmas de sus manos, sus rodillas y las puntas de los dedos de sus pies en el suelo diciendo «»Subhana Rabial A›ala= Glorificado sea mi Señor el Altísimo»» tres veces.

passages.heading: ¿Cómo realizar la ablución mayor (Ghusl)?
passages.text:
Al realizar la ablución mayor (ghusl) debe lavarse todo el cuerpo con agua, además de realizar el enjuague y la inhalación, y de este modo el musulmán habrá realizado la purificación mayor.

Al Hadaz Al Akbar: es lo que exige una purificación mayor y no se quita con solo realizar la ablución menor (wudu), y es de tres tipos:

1. Al Yanaba (estado de impureza mayor): es un estado que acompaña el coito o la eyaculación con deseo aunque no se haya dado el coito.
2. La menstruación: es la sangre que sale mensualmente de la mujer.
3. El postparto: es la sangre que sale de la mujer después del parto.

passages.heading: ¿Cuándo es obligatoria la ablución mayor (ghusl)?
passages.text:
El musulmán debe realizar la ablución mayor (ghusl) en tres casos:

- **El primero:** la eyaculación con deseo, sea si eyacula estando despierto o dormido.
- **El segundo:** el coito, si hay eyaculación o no.
- **Tercero:** la sangre de la menstruación o el postparto de la mujer, y cuando se termina debe realizar la ablución mayor.

passages.heading: A discutir
passages.text: ¿Qué indica la purificación mayor para salir del Hadaz Al Akbar (estado de impureza mayor)?

passages.heading: Lo prohibido en el estado de impureza mayor:
passages.text:
El estado de la persona que necesita realizar la ablución mayor por el coito o por la eyaculación se llama (Yanaba) y a la persona se le llama (Yunub) y en este estado lo está prohibido lo siguiente:

1. La oración.
2. La circunvalación alrededor del Kaaba.
3. Tocar o llevar el Libro del Corán.
4. Quedarse en la mezquita.
5. La recitación del Noble Corán.

passages.heading: Los tipos de sangre que sale de la mujer:
passages.text:
La sangre que sale de la mujer es de dos tipos:

| La sangre de la menstruación: | La sangre del postparto: |
| :--- | :--- |
| es un sangrado natural que sale del útero de la mujer generalmente cada mes, y dura unos días y se llama (menstruación). | es la sangre natural que sale del útero de la mujer después del parto del feto, y queda hasta 40 días (depende de cada mujer). |

passages.heading: Normas relacionadas con la menstruación y el posparto.
passages.text: ■ La ablución mayor (ghusl) cuando se detiene el sangrado, así es que cuando se termina el período de menstruación o del postparto la mujer debe realizar la ablución mayor (como fue explicado anteriormente).

passages.heading: A discutir

passages.heading: ¿Por qué debo volverme musulmán?
passages.text:
Algunos pueden preguntarse: ¿Por qué tengo que convertirme al Islam?

Y la respuesta es: debo ser musulmán por las razones siguientes:

La primera: el Islam es la sola religión aceptada por Al-láh a sus siervos y no aceptará ninguna aparte de ella. Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:3:85}} Corán (3: 85).

La segunda: el Islam es la religión de todos los profetas, invita a creer en todos ellos, sin discriminar entre ellos. Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:2:136}} Corán (2:136).

La diferencia entre los profetas consiste en una diferencia de legislaciones relacionadas con las acciones de las personas, por ello Al-láh- Glorificado sea- dijo: {{Q:5:48}} Corán (5: 48).

Es decir: cada nación tiene una legisalción propia, una manera propia para acercarse a Al-láh con la adoración, entonces cada nación tiene normas legales propias, pero el credo de todos los profetas es igual y no cambia.

Tercero: Convertirse al Islam es el camino a la felicidad en esta vida y a la salvación en la otra vida, ya que no se salva en la otra vida sino quien al recibir el mensaje del profeta Muhammad -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- haya creído en él y le haya seguido, Al-láh-Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:3:85}} Corán (3: 85)

El profeta -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- dijo:» Juro por Aquel que posee mi alma en Su mano que, si una persona de este pueblo sea judío o cristiano, oye mi Mensaje y muere sin haber creído en él, será de la gente del infierno». Narrado por Muslim 153.

Cuarto: El Islam responde con respuestas evidentes a mis preguntas: ¿Por qué estoy en esta vida? ¿De dónde vine? y ¿A dónde iré después de la muerte?

Quinto: El Islam es una religión que coincide con la inclinación natural del ser humano, desde el valor más importante que presenta -que es el Monoteísmo- hasta llegar a los buenos modales hacia los cuales invita.

passages.heading: A discutir
passages.text: ¿Cómo puede ser que el Islam sea la religión de todos los profetas?

passages.heading: Roupas proibidas:
passages.text:
Os limites da parte privada de um homem é do umbigo ao joelho. Quanto à mulher, é tudo awrah na frente de homens não mahram. Quanto aos seus mahrams, como pai, filho e irmão, ela mostra a ele o que ela mostra na frente das mulheres, incluindo o rosto, cabelo, pescoço, braços e pernas.

ALLAH Todo-Poderoso proibiu vários tipos de roupas, incluindo:

- O que expõe as partes íntimas e não as cobre.
- O que imita o sexo oposto; Os homens usam roupas femininas, ou as mulheres usam roupas masculinas.
- O que o faz sentir orgulho e vaidade.
- O que mostra extravagância e desperdício.
- É proibido aos homens usar seda e usar ouro e prata.
- É proibido usar qualquer coisa que imite as roupas dos infiéis, como as roupas de padres e monges, por exemplo.

Compartilhe com seus colegas para conhecer alguns dos motivos da proibição de tipos de vestuário.

passages.heading: O véu da mulher muçulmana:
passages.text: ALLAH impôs o véu à mulher, não ao homem, por causa da beleza e dos fatores sedutores que estão depositados nela, o que faz dela uma tentação para o homem mais do que um homem seja uma tentação para ela. Os limites deste véu são cobrir todo o seu corpo de homens estranhos, e ela pode usar as formas e cores que quiser, respeitando quatro condições:

passages.heading: A relação de uma mulher com um homem:
passages.text: O relacionamento de uma mulher com um homem é dividido em três partes:

passages.heading: Faça parte de seu mahram:
passages.text: O que se entende por mahrams é todo aquele que é terminantemente proibido a um homem se casar com ela, tais como: a mãe, a irmã, a filha da irmã, a filha do irmão, a irmã do pai, a irmã da mãe e a mãe da esposa. É permitido que elas saiam na frente de seus mahrams com seus adornos que mostram os braços, pescoço, cabelos, e assim por diante, sem culpa ou excessos.

passages.heading: 2 O Islam apaga o que precedeu de pecados
passages.text:
Quando a pessoa abraça um verdadeiro Islam; ALLAH, o Clemente, o Misericordioso, perdoa todos os seus pecados passados, e esta é uma das belezas do Islam. O Todo-Poderoso disse ao Seu Profeta ﷺ: {{Q:8:38}} [Al-Anfal: 38]

Um homem veio querendo se submeter ao Profeta, que a paz e as bênçãos de ALLAH estejam com ele, mas ele estipulou que ele fosse perdoado pelo que havia passado, então ele, que a paz e bênçãos de ALLAH estejam com ele, deu-lhe boas novas e disse-lhe: Acaso não sabes que o Islam apaga o que antecedeu? Musslim 121

passages.heading: Regras de animais em restaurantes e lojas:
passages.text:
1. O que foi sacrificado por um não-muçulmano ou um cristão (judeu ou cristão); Como budistas, hindus e pessoas não religiosas, isso é proibido e inclui o que é encontrado em restaurantes e lojas em países cujos residentes são principalmente não-muçulmanos nem pessoas do livro.
2. O que um muçulmano ou um do povo do livro abate à maneira islâmica, isso é permitido de acordo com o texto do Alcorão.
3. O que um muçulmano ou cristão mata ilegalmente, como eletrocussão ou afogamento, é proibido.
4. O princípio básico é que é permitido consumir o que um judeu ou cristão sacrificou e é oferecido em seus restaurantes e lojas, com o cuidado de mencionar o nome de ALLAH ao comer. É melhor para um muçulmano não comer nada, exceto o que é verificado como carne permitida e halal.

passages.heading: O critério de superioridade no Islam
passages.text:
ALLAH Todo-Poderoso fez o critério para a diferenciação entre Seus servos em fé e piedade, de modo que a distinção entre os muçulmanos é baseada na força de sua fé, e não em suas formas, nem sua linhagem, nem suas cores, nem seu dinheiro, como o Todo-Poderoso disse: {{Q:49:13}} [Al-Hujurát:13]

E o Profeta ﷺ disse: “Ó gente, vosso Senhor é um e vosso pai é um. Não há superioridade de um árabe em relação a um não árabe, nem de um não árabe em relação a um árabe, e nem pele branca sobre pele negra, nem pele negra sobre pele branca, exceto pelo temor. Narrado por Baihaqi no (livro) Shuab al-íman 4774/2619

passages.heading: Roupas proibidas:
passages.text: O Mensageiro, que a paz e as bênçãos estejam com ele, proibiu os homens de imitar mulheres e mulheres aos homens. Essa proibição inclui o tipo de vestimenta e a maneira de falar. Essa imitação é um grande pecado que exige punição de ALLAH para quem o faz e não se arrependa disso.O Islam quer que a natureza do homem e sua aparência sejam distintas da natureza da mulher, assim como para a mulher; É a evidência do bom senso e da lógica correta.

passages.text: Uma mulher estranha é toda mulher que não é um de seus mahrams, seja ela uma de suas parentes, como a filha de um de seus tios, a esposa de seu irmão e parentes do sexo feminino da família, ou ela não seja sua parente e ele não tem uma relação familiar com ela, e o Islam estabeleceu regras para lidar entre os sexos, como a obrigação do hijab e não estar sozinho.

passages.text: É permitido a eles olhar e desfrutar o que a outros não são permitidos, e ALLAH nomeou o marido como uma vestimenta para a esposa e a esposa como uma vestimenta para o marido, como uma imagem maravilhosa do contato psicológico, emocional e físico entre eles.

passages.heading: Qual é a decisão sobre comer animais marinhos?
passages.text:
Animais aquáticos que vivem apenas na água, é permitido comer seus mortos, como peixes e camarões e assim por diante, quer vivam em mares, rios ou lagos.

É permitido caçar e comer animais selvagens que não sejam predatórios, desde que o nome de ALLAH seja mencionado durante a caça e abatido se os encontrar vivos.

passages.heading: Pilares do Islam
passages.text:

O Islam é composto por cinco pilares:
